html: Nearly everything your body does depends on water, from keeping you cool to helping you digest food. Needs vary with your size, activity and the weather, so no single number fits everyone.

• Carry a bottle you like and refill it through the day
  • Have a glass with each meal
  • Add a slice of citrus or cucumber for flavor
  • Water-rich foods like melon, soup and leafy greens count too
Thirst, darker urine, a dry mouth or a headache on a hot day can all be hints to drink up. People with heart or kidney conditions should ask their care team how much is right for them.

title: Staying hydrated
abstract: Why fluids matter, easy ways to drink more and signs you might need extra.
